quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian embroidery is one of the most colorful folk art traditions in Europe, with each region having its own distinctive patterns and colors. The town of Kalocsa is especially famous for its vibrant floral designs in red, blue, and yellow, which decorate everything from tablecloths to traditional costumes. These beautiful patterns have been passed down through generations of Hungarian women.

short_read.title: The Secret Language of Trees
short_read.teaser: Scientists have discovered that trees in a forest communicate with each other through an underground network of fungi. Mother trees even nurture their young seedlings by sending them nutrients through these natural pathways.

medium_read.title: The Return of Sea Otters to the Pacific Northwest
medium_read.teaser: After nearly disappearing from Washington waters, sea otters are making a remarkable comeback along the Olympic Coast. Their return is helping restore the health of kelp forests and the entire marine ecosystem.

long_read.title: The Lighthouse Keepers of the Strait of Juan de Fuca
long_read.teaser: For over a century, brave families tended the lighthouses that guided ships through the treacherous waters between Washington and Vancouver Island. Their stories of isolation, dedication, and dramatic rescues paint a vivid picture of maritime life in the Pacific Northwest.

port_angeles.title: Roosevelt Elk in Olympic National Park
port_angeles.description: August is a wonderful time to spot Roosevelt elk in the Hoh Rain Forest and along the coastal areas of Olympic National Park. These magnificent animals, named after President Theodore Roosevelt, are the largest of the four surviving subspecies of elk in North America. Early morning and evening hours offer the best viewing opportunities.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute while flying.
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's right, Barbara! Hummingbirds have incredibly fast heartbeats to power their amazing flying abilities!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute — that's amazingly fast!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: A hummingbird's tiny heart actually beats about 1,200 times per minute! That's what gives them the energy to hover and dart so quickly.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To fuel this incredible heart rate, hummingbirds must eat about half their body weight in nectar each day and visit hundreds of flowers. Their metabolism is so fast that they can starve to death in just a few hours if they can't find food.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'thank you'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Köszönöm! That's absolutely right, Barbara! Such a lovely word to know.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The word for 'thank you' in Hungarian is 'köszönöm' — such a beautiful and important word in any language!
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is part of the Finno-Ugric language family, making it quite different from most other European languages. It's known for its long words and complex grammar, but also for its beautiful sound and expressive nature.

puzzle_3.question: What unique feature helps harbor seals, common in the Strait of Juan de Fuca, see clearly underwater?
options: They close their eyes and use whiskers
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! Harbor seals can actually change the shape of their lenses to see clearly both in and out of water — nature's amazing engineering!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Harbor seals have a remarkable ability to change the shape of their eye lenses, allowing them to see clearly both underwater and on land. It's one of nature's most clever adaptations!
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Harbor seals are year-round residents of the Strait of Juan de Fuca and can often be spotted resting on rocks near Port Angeles. Their whiskers are also incredibly sensitive, helping them detect fish movements even in murky water.
